papers.title: From RNA design to delivery: Computational strategies for functional RNA therapeutics.
papers.abstract: RNA therapeutics provide a revolutionary means of treating a variety of diseases by precisely regulating gene expression and protein synthesis, with great medical significance. However, there are three key challenges to its clinical application: the inherent instability of RNA, the need for controlled regulation of RNA function, and the lack of an efficient delivery system. Computational strategies provide complementary tools for analyzing and optimizing RNA sequence, structure, function, and delivery, accelerating the rational design of RNAs and the optimization of delivery systems. This revi
papers.summary: This review surveys computational strategies that address the three main barriers to RNA therapeutics: RNA instability, the need for controllable RNA function, and inefficient delivery. It covers how computational tools for analyzing and optimizing RNA sequence, structure, and function can accelerate rational RNA design and delivery-system optimization.

papers.title: Hybrid density functional study of strain-engineered III-V semiconductors and monolayer InSe.
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of strain-dependent semiconductor properties requires reliable exchange-correlation treatments and a unified understanding of bulk and two-dimensional materials. Here, we investigate strain-engineered bulk AlP, AlSb, and monolayer InSe under biaxial strains from -6% to +6% using the Perdew-Burke-Ernzerhof (PBE) and Heyd-Scuseria-Ernzerhof (HSE06) functionals. HSE06 significantly improves structural accuracy, reducing the mean absolute deviation in lattice parameters from 1.47% to 0.39%. Biaxial strain lowers the symmetry of bulk AlP and AlSb from cubic zinc blende to tetrag
papers.summary: This study uses hybrid density functional theory (HSE06) to model how biaxial strain affects the electronic and structural properties of bulk AlP, AlSb, and monolayer InSe. HSE06 substantially improves lattice parameter accuracy over standard PBE, reducing mean absolute deviation from 1.47% to 0.39%, and reveals strain-induced symmetry lowering in the bulk III-V compounds. The work provides a more reliable computational framework for predicting strain-tunable semiconductor behavior across bulk and 2D materials.

papers.title: Bidirectional crosstalk between the catalytic and moonlighting functions of human dipeptidyl peptidase 3: potential physiological implications.
papers.abstract: Dipeptidyl peptidase 3 (DPP3) is a ubiquitously expressed zinc-exopeptidase involved in oligopeptide degradation. Beyond its catalytic role, DPP3 exhibits a moonlighting role in the Keap1-Nrf2 signalling pathway, where it promotes Nrf2-dependent gene transcription through an ETGE motif-mediated interaction with the Kelch domain of Keap1. This highlights its role in oxidative stress and cancer, as persistent pathway activation supports tumour cell survival, oxidative stress resistance, and proliferation. While DPP3's catalytic activity is not required for Keap1 binding, the effects of enzyme in
papers.summary: This study examines how the catalytic (peptide-cleaving) and moonlighting (Keap1-binding) functions of human dipeptidyl peptidase 3 (DPP3) influence each other. The authors find bidirectional crosstalk between these two roles, suggesting that DPP3's enzymatic activity and its regulation of the Keap1-Nrf2 oxidative stress pathway are interconnected, with potential physiological implications for cancer and stress responses.

papers.title: Structural Overview of GLP-1 Analogs.
papers.abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) analogs exert potent metabolic effects through structural features that govern receptor engagement, signaling, and pharmacokinetics. Key structural determinants include N-terminal modifications that confer resistance to dipeptidyl peptidase-4 degradation, as well as C-terminal and backbone elements that stabilize peptide helicity and enhance GLP-1 receptor affinity. Lipidation and albumin-binding strategies prolong systemic exposure by increasing circulating half-life, forming the basis of long-acting agents such as liraglutide and semaglutide. Structural variat
papers.summary: This review examines how the structural features of GLP-1 analogs—such as N-terminal modifications that resist DPP-4 degradation, C-terminal and backbone elements that stabilize helicity, and lipidation/albumin-binding strategies—determine receptor engagement, signaling, and pharmacokinetics. These structural insights explain the design of long-acting agents like liraglutide and semaglutide.

papers.title: Engineered Transformer Base Editor with Enhanced Editing Efficiency.
papers.abstract: Canonical cytosine base editors (CBEs) achieve precise C-to-T conversions without inducing DNA double-strand breaks (DSBs), yet their clinical potential remains hampered by substantial off-target (OT) mutations. The recently developed transformer base editor (tBE) significantly reduces both genomic and transcriptomic OT mutations by using a cleavable deoxycytidine deaminase inhibitor (dCDI) domain. However, the modest base editing efficiency limits its broader applications. Here, through rational deaminase engineering and fusion of a uracil DNA glycosylase inhibitor (UGI) domain, we developed
papers.summary: The authors engineered an improved transformer base editor (tBE) that retains its low off-target mutation profile while achieving substantially higher C-to-T editing efficiency. This was accomplished through rational engineering of the deaminase and fusion of a uracil DNA glycosylase inhibitor (UGI) domain. The work addresses a key limitation of the original tBE, potentially broadening its therapeutic applicability.

papers.title: Pharmacological modulation of GPR84 revealed by dual states structures and immune functional assays.
papers.abstract: G-protein-coupled receptor 84 (GPR84) is an orphan class A GPCR selectively activated by medium chain fatty acids and highly expressed in immune cells, where it modulates pro-inflammatory signaling. The structural basis of GPR84 inactivation and antagonism has remained unclear, limiting the rational design of pathway-selective modulators despite its clinical relevance in metabolic inflammation and fibrotic diseases. Here, we report cryo-electron microscopy structures of human GPR84 in inactive and active states. The 3.5 Å inactive structure bound to the antagonist GLPG1205 reveals a lid-like c
papers.summary: This study presents cryo-EM structures of the orphan GPCR GPR84 in both inactive (bound to antagonist GLPG1205) and active states, revealing the structural basis for receptor inactivation and antagonism. Combined with immune functional assays, the work identifies key conformational changes and provides a framework for designing pathway-selective modulators for inflammatory and fibrotic diseases.

papers.title: Biological Investigation of Novel Pyrazole-Based Anticancer Scaffolds: A Trinity of Synthetic Methodologies on Computational Assessment of IC50 Against Human Cancer Cell Lines MCF-7, MDA-MB and HeLa.
papers.abstract: Aurora kinase A (AURKA) is a key regulator of mitotic progression and is frequently overexpressed in human malignancies, making it an attractive therapeutic target for the development of targeted anticancer agents. The present study aimed to design and synthesize sixteen novel pyrazole derivatives (Pz-01 to Pz-16) as potential AURKA-targeted anticancer agents and to evaluate their anticancer activity, AURKA-binding potential, and SAR using integrated experimental and computational approaches. The synthesized compounds were screened for cytotoxic activity against human breast cancer (MCF-7 and
papers.journal: European journal of pharmaceutical sciences : official journal of the European Federation for Pharmaceutical Sciences
papers.summary: This study designed and synthesized sixteen novel pyrazole derivatives as potential inhibitors of Aurora kinase A (AURKA), a mitotic regulator overexpressed in many cancers. The compounds were tested for cytotoxicity against breast cancer (MCF-7, MDA-MB) and cervical cancer (HeLa) cell lines, with computational docking and SAR analysis used to assess AURKA binding and guide structure-activity relationships.

papers.title: Domain-Swapped LuxR-Type Quorum Sensing Receptors Reveal Divergent Ligand-Response Mechanisms among Homologues.
papers.abstract: LuxI/R quorum sensing controls diverse cell density-dependent behaviors in gram-negative bacteria, yet the molecular basis of LuxR-type receptor response to ligands remains poorly defined. This gap limits both mechanistic understanding of signaling and the rational design of synthetic LuxR modulators. LuxR homologues exhibit two response modes: associative receptors require N-acyl l-homoserine lactone (AHL) signal binding to enable DNA binding and transcriptional activation, whereas dissociative receptors are active without ligand and inhibited upon AHL binding. Herein, we dissect determinants
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.summary: This study dissects how LuxR-type quorum sensing receptors respond to ligands by creating domain-swapped chimeric receptors between associative and dissociative homologues. The authors identify specific protein domains that determine whether ligand binding activates or inhibits DNA binding, revealing divergent molecular mechanisms among closely related receptors. This provides a framework for engineering synthetic LuxR modulators with tailored ligand responses.

papers.title: Rational Design of Au@co-MOF Synergistic Platform for Ultrasensitive Monitoring of Dopamine in Human Biological Fluids.
papers.abstract: This study presents the rational design and application of engineered metal-organic framework (MOF) hybrids, tailored to exhibit accelerated electron transfer kinetics and enhanced molecular recognition capabilities for the high-sensitivity detection of dopamine (DA). Specifically, an enzyme-free electrochemical sensing platform was constructed using Au@Co-MOF nanocomposites, which were synthesized via a controllable in situ growth approach. Au nanoparticles (AuNPs) were uniformly anchored onto the [Co3(TMA)3(H2O)5]n (where TMA = 1,3,5-trimesic acid) framework containing coordinatively unsatur
papers.summary: This study describes an enzyme-free electrochemical sensor built from gold nanoparticles anchored onto a cobalt-based metal-organic framework (Au@Co-MOF) for detecting dopamine in human biological fluids. The hybrid platform shows accelerated electron transfer and enhanced molecular recognition, enabling ultrasensitive dopamine quantification. The work is a materials-engineering contribution to biosensing rather than a biological discovery.

papers.title: In Silico Identification of Novel Leads as Potential DPP-IV Inhibitors as Antidiabetic Agents Using Virtual Screening.
papers.abstract: Purpose: Dipeptidyl peptidase-IV (DPP-IV) is a validated therapeutic target for type 2 diabetes mellitus due to its role in incretin hormone degradation. This study aimed to identify novel small-molecule DPP-IV inhibitors from the ECBD database using an integrated virtual screening and molecular dynamics (MD) approach, acknowledging that experimental validation is necessary to confirm biological activity. Methods: Structure-based virtual screening of 5,500 ECBD compounds was performed using molecular docking to identify high-affinity ligands, followed by interaction analysis with key catalytic
papers.summary: This study used molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations to screen 5,500 compounds from the ECBD database for potential inhibitors of DPP-IV, a validated target for type 2 diabetes. Several high-affinity lead compounds were identified through interaction analysis with key catalytic residues, though the authors note that experimental validation is needed to confirm biological activity.

papers.title: Cross-docking and redocking reveal distinct determinants of success in physics-based and AI-driven binding pose prediction in protein-ligand complexes.
papers.abstract: Protein-ligand pose prediction is central to structure-based drug discovery, yet the relative performance of physics-based and AI-driven methods under realistic cross-docking conditions remains insufficiently characterized. Here, we compare physics-based docking methods (AutoDock4, AutoDock Vina, and DOCK 6) with data-driven approaches, including the deep-learning model GNINA 1.3 and the diffusion-based frameworks AlphaFold 3, Boltz-2, and DiffDock. Performance was evaluated using standardised redocking and cross-docking protocols across three Alzheimer's disease targets representing distinct
papers.summary: This study benchmarks physics-based docking tools (AutoDock4, AutoDock Vina, DOCK 6) against AI-driven pose predictors (GNINA 1.3, AlphaFold 3, Boltz-2, DiffDock) under both redocking and cross-docking conditions on three Alzheimer's disease targets. The authors find that the two paradigms have distinct determinants of success, with AI methods performing well in redocking but showing different strengths and weaknesses than physics-based methods under realistic cross-docking scenarios.

papers.title: Structure-based design of soluble prefusion-stabilized herpes simplex virus type 2 glycoprotein B antigens.
papers.abstract: Herpes simplex virus type 2 (HSV-2) infection causes recurrent genital herpes throughout life, yet no vaccines have been approved. Glycoprotein B (gB) is a class III fusion protein that mediates HSV-2 entry by transitioning from a metastable prefusion conformation to a stable postfusion conformation. Here, using structure-based design, we stabilize HSV-2 gB in its prefusion conformation. A 2.8 Å resolution cryo-EM structure reveals a closed state of prefusion gB, which differs from recently published open states. Vaccination of mice with protein subunit and mRNA-based vaccines of pre- and post
papers.summary: This study uses structure-based design to engineer soluble, prefusion-stabilized glycoprotein B (gB) antigens for herpes simplex virus type 2 (HSV-2), a major cause of recurrent genital herpes with no approved vaccine. A 2.8 Å cryo-EM structure revealed a closed prefusion gB conformation distinct from previously reported open states, and vaccination of mice with protein subunit and mRNA vaccines based on these antigens elicited immune responses. The work provides a promising vaccine design strategy for HSV-2.

papers.title: Enhanced Line Search Improves Robustness and Efficiency of Pose Sampling in Protein-Ligand Docking.
papers.abstract: Physics-based protein-ligand docking critically depends on efficient pose sampling, yet established sampling and local refinement algorithms can be inefficient and unstable in the highly nonconvex energy landscapes characteristic of protein-ligand interactions. To address this limitation, we introduce an enhanced local optimization strategy based on curved line search (CLS) and integrate it into AutoDock Vina, resulting in Vina_CLS. The proposed method enables more flexible step-size selection during local refinement and improves convergence in challenging regions of the energy landscape. Acro
papers.journal: Journal of chemical theory and computation
papers.summary: The authors introduce a curved line search (CLS) optimization strategy integrated into AutoDock Vina (Vina_CLS) to improve pose sampling in protein-ligand docking. This approach enables more flexible step-size selection during local refinement, improving convergence in the highly nonconvex energy landscapes typical of protein-ligand interactions. The method aims to enhance both robustness and efficiency of docking pose generation.

papers.title: Enhancing prediction accuracy for enzyme activity engineering through sequence co-evolution and epistatic relationship modeling.
papers.abstract: Conventional enzyme engineering strategies, such as directed evolution with structure-based analysis, are limited by laborious workflows and by the need to screen extensive enzyme libraries. Computational models based on multiple sequence alignment, such as SCANEER, have streamlined these engineering strategies, enabling the successful prediction of single-site mutations that enhance enzyme activity. However, when combining predicted mutations to improve enzyme performance or expand mutational space, such approaches often fail due to epistatic interactions among amino acid residues, which can
papers.summary: This paper presents a computational approach that improves prediction of enzyme activity-enhancing mutations by incorporating sequence co-evolution and epistatic relationships, addressing a key limitation of existing tools like SCANEER that struggle when combining individually beneficial mutations. The method aims to reduce experimental screening burden in enzyme engineering by better modeling how mutations interact.

papers.title: ProRB: a structure-free unified framework for joint prediction and design of protein-RNA interactions.
papers.abstract: While protein-RNA interactions are fundamental to post-transcriptional processes, achieving a holistic understanding of their regulatory logic remains challenging. Current computational models often treat binding affinity, interface mapping, and RNA design as isolated tasks, thereby failing to provide a unified perspective of the protein-RNA interactome. Here, we introduce ProRB, a unified sequence-based framework that jointly estimates protein-RNA binding affinity, predicts binding interfaces in proteins and RNAs, and generates protein-binding RNA sequences from protein sequences. By fusing p
papers.summary: ProRB is a unified, sequence-based computational framework that jointly predicts protein-RNA binding affinity, maps binding interfaces on both proteins and RNAs, and designs protein-binding RNA sequences directly from protein sequences. Unlike prior models that treat these tasks separately, ProRB offers a holistic view of the protein-RNA interactome without requiring structural input.

papers.title: Prediction of Ocular Toxicity of Prostaglandin F2α Analogs Based on Local Computational Models: Superiority over Global Models and Experimental Validation.
papers.abstract: Drug-induced ocular toxicity is difficult to predict and evaluate, particularly for prostaglandin F2α (PGF2α) analogs used in the management of glaucoma. Traditional global predictive models, which are built with large and various datasets (n = 6187), provide systematic false-negative results for groups of structurally uniform compounds. To address this limitation, we developed special local classification models for PGF2α analogs. A structurally consistent local training dataset (n = 350) was assembled using Murcko scaffold filtering and Tanimoto similarity selection (≥0.5). Binary classifica
papers.summary: This study shows that local computational models trained on structurally similar prostaglandin F2α analogs outperform global models in predicting ocular toxicity, which global models systematically underestimate for this compound class. The authors built a focused dataset of 350 compounds using scaffold filtering and similarity selection, and validated their predictions experimentally.

papers.title: Characterizing CCR2 homodimers using homology-derived and AI-predicted interfaces.
papers.abstract: Deciphering the functional roles of G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) oligomers requires defining their structural organization, which remains a challenge due to the inherent flexibility of their 7 transmembrane (TM) domains. Here, we focused on determining homodimer interfaces of the chemokine receptor CCR2, a major component of the inflammatory response, for which no antagonist has yet been approved. We generated models of CCR2 homodimers combining homology modeling, a conventional in silico approach, or an AI-based AlphaFold-Multimer predictions, with molecular dynamics simulations. We de
papers.summary: This study models the homodimer interfaces of the chemokine receptor CCR2 using two complementary approaches: traditional homology modeling and AI-based AlphaFold-Multimer predictions, both refined with molecular dynamics simulations. The work aims to clarify how CCR2 self-associates structurally, which is relevant for understanding its role in inflammation and for future drug development.

papers.title: Integrated Pharmacogenomic and Structure-Guided Analyses Link LCC-10 (NSC765599) to an MMP-Associated Extracellular Matrix Regulatory Network in Leukemia.
papers.abstract: Leukemia progression is increasingly shaped by reciprocal interactions between leukemic cells and the bone marrow microenvironment, yet the extracellular regulatory networks associated with these interactions remain incompletely understood. Here, we investigated the biological context associated with the antileukemic activity of LCC-10 (NSC765599), a synthetic biphenyl benzamide derivative, using an integrated pharmacogenomic and structure-guided computational framework. Antiproliferative activity was first characterized using the NCI-60 screen and subsequently integrated with pharmacogenomic
papers.summary: This study uses integrated pharmacogenomic and structure-guided computational analyses to link the antileukemic compound LCC-10 (NSC765599) to an MMP-associated extracellular matrix regulatory network in leukemia. The authors characterize its antiproliferative activity via the NCI-60 screen and connect it to leukemia-microenvironment interactions, suggesting a potential therapeutic target context.

papers.title: Molecular Dynamics Study on Solution Transport Properties in CSH/SiO2 Nanochannels Under High-Temperature and Water-Rich Environments.
papers.abstract: This study employs molecular dynamics simulations to construct a CSH/SiO2 nanochannel model, systematically investigating the dynamic transport behavior of pure water and Na2SO4 solution within the pores across temperatures ranging from 293 K to 368 K. The results elucidate the fluid intrusion mechanism under the combined effects of elevated temperature and sulfate ions. Results show that: (i) Water migration within the CSH/SiO2 channel exhibits wall-dependent differences. The interaction between water and the CSH surface is approximately eight times stronger than with the SiO2 side at 293 K,
papers.summary: This study uses molecular dynamics simulations to model water and Na2SO4 solution transport through CSH/SiO2 nanochannels at temperatures from 293 K to 368 K. It finds that water interacts with the CSH surface roughly eight times more strongly than with the SiO2 surface at 293 K, revealing wall-dependent migration behavior and the combined effects of temperature and sulfate ions on fluid intrusion.

papers.title: Antimicrobial peptides as computational candidates for SARS-CoV-2 papain-like protease inhibition.
papers.abstract: SARS-CoV-2 papain-like protease (PLpro) remains an attractive antiviral target because of its dual role in viral polyprotein processing and host immune modulation. In this study, we employed an exploratory structure-based computational workflow to identify antimicrobial peptide scaffolds with predicted PLpro-binding potential. A total of 6,615 peptides compiled from public databases were screened using protein-peptide docking, followed by molecular dynamics simulations and end-state binding energy analysis for selected complexes. Among the prioritized candidates, peptides 33,035 and 17,047 sho
papers.summary: This study used computational docking and molecular dynamics simulations to screen 6,615 antimicrobial peptides from public databases for potential binding to the SARS-CoV-2 papain-like protease (PLpro), an antiviral drug target. Two peptides (33,035 and 17,047) emerged as top candidates with favorable predicted binding energies, suggesting they warrant further experimental validation as PLpro inhibitors.

papers.title: Drug Design Studio (DDS) 2.0: A Unified Platform for Network Pharmacology Integrated with Docking and Virtual Screening Workflow for Covalent/Non-Covalent Binders.
papers.abstract: Network pharmacology has become a central paradigm in modern drug discovery, replacing the reductionist "one drug, one target" view with a systems-level understanding of how compounds engage networks of proteins that are linked to disease. Despite its impact, a typical network-pharmacology study remains fragmented and technically demanding: researchers must query several independent databases, install and reconcile multiple standalone tools for target collection, network construction, hub-gene ranking and pathway enrichment, and then manually bridge the results into structure-based follow-up s
papers.summary: The authors present Drug Design Studio (DDS) 2.0, an integrated software platform that unifies network pharmacology analysis with molecular docking and virtual screening for both covalent and non-covalent binders. It aims to replace the fragmented workflow of querying multiple databases and standalone tools by providing a single environment for target collection, network construction, hub-gene ranking, pathway enrichment, and structure-based follow-up.

papers.title: Substrate Recognition Analysis in an Ethyl Carbamate-Hydrolyzing Esterase and Semi-Rational Baijiu Flavor Preservation.
papers.abstract: Ethyl carbamate (EC) is a widely recognized carcinogen present in fermented foods, and enzymatic degradation is a safe and effective strategy for its reduction. An EC-degrading esterase derived from Acinetobacter calcoaceticus (AcECH) was previously identified. However, volatile ester compounds in Chinese Baijiu compete with EC for enzyme binding, thereby affecting degradation efficiency and flavor quality. In this study, molecular docking, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, enzyme kinetics, bio-layer interferometry (BLI), and gas chromatography-ion mobility spectrometry (GC-IMS) were employ
papers.summary: This study investigates how an ethyl carbamate-degrading esterase (AcECH) from Acinetobacter calcoaceticus interacts with competing volatile esters in Chinese Baijiu, using molecular docking, MD simulations, enzyme kinetics, BLI, and GC-IMS. The goal is to understand substrate recognition and enable semi-rational engineering to preserve flavor while reducing the carcinogen ethyl carbamate.

papers.title: Integrative In Silico Profiling of Major Phytochemicals From a Sclerocarya birrea-Nauclea latifolia-Piper longum Mixture: Docking, Molecular Dynamics, ADMET, and Ligand-Based Target Prediction on Shared Pathways in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus and Alzheimer's Disease.
papers.abstract: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and Alzheimer's disease (AD) converge through metabolic dysfunction, inflammation, and impaired neuronal signaling, providing a rationale for multi-target intervention. This study aimed to identify phytochemicals from a Sclerocarya birrea-Nauclea latifolia-Piper longum mixture that may modulate this disease axis. Seven constituents were screened against AChE, BACE1, DPP4, glucokinase, GSK3β, and TACE using molecular docking and MM-GBSA rescoring. Prioritized complexes underwent triplicate 100-ns molecular dynamics simulations, post-MD MM-GBSA analysis, physicoch
papers.summary: This study used computational docking, molecular dynamics, and ADMET profiling to screen seven phytochemicals from a three-plant mixture against six protein targets shared between type 2 diabetes and Alzheimer's disease. The authors identified prioritized compounds with favorable binding and drug-like properties that may modulate the shared metabolic-inflammatory axis. The work is entirely in silico and provides hypotheses for future experimental validation rather than direct biological evidence.

papers.title: Engineering the Stability of Sucrose Synthase to Enable Efficient Coupled Production of UDP-Glucuronic Acid.
papers.abstract: The biocatalytic synthesis of UDP-glucuronic acid (UDPGA), a key precursor for glucuronides and high-value carbohydrates, is limited by an unstable UDP-glucose (UDPG) supply in coupled systems. In this study, through an extensive screening of 10 sucrose synthases derived from both eukaryotic and prokaryotic microorganisms, we identified a broad-spectrum, highly efficient enzymatic scaffold suitable for the synthesis of UDP-sugars. A rational design integrating PROSS and ThermoMPNN algorithms with molecular dynamics (MD) analysis yielded the V353L mutant, which retained 97% of wild-type activit
papers.summary: This study screened 10 sucrose synthases to find a stable enzyme for producing UDP-glucuronic acid, a valuable precursor for glucuronides and carbohydrates. Using computational design (PROSS, ThermoMPNN, and MD simulations), they engineered a V353L mutant that retained 97% of wild-type activity while improving stability, enabling more efficient coupled production of UDPGA.

papers.title: Preparation, Structural Features, Bioactivities, and Food Application of Oyster Mushroom Polysaccharides: A Review.
papers.abstract: Water-soluble oyster mushroom polysaccharides (OMPs) are multifunctional biopolymers with growing relevance in food and health-related applications. This review summarizes recent progress in the extraction, purification, structural features, biological activities, and food applications of OMPs, with particular emphasis on tentative structure-activity relationships constrained by heterogeneous experimental evidence. Conventional and emerging extraction approaches, including hot water, enzyme-assisted, ultrasound-assisted, and microwave-assisted methods, are compared in terms of yield and struct
papers.summary: This review consolidates recent research on water-soluble polysaccharides from oyster mushrooms, covering extraction and purification methods, structural characterization, biological activities, and food applications. It highlights tentative structure-activity relationships while noting that heterogeneous experimental evidence limits firm conclusions. The work serves as a reference for researchers and food scientists interested in these multifunctional biopolymers.

papers.title: Recent Exploration of Right-Handed D-Sulfonyl-γ-AApeptides as Potential Tools Toward α-Helical Mimicry.
papers.abstract: Over the last 15 years, our laboratory has explored peptidomimetics in diverse research areas, including AApeptide folding, structure-based design, combinatorial screening, and supramolecular chemistry. Through these efforts, we successfully introduced a new subclass of AApeptides known as sulfonyl-γ-AApeptides. In recent years, we took advantage of the synthetic scaffold and rationally designed and developed helices targeting a series of protein-protein interactions. This Perspective summarizes our recent advances in developing right-handed helical D-sulfonyl-γ-AApeptides, which closely resem
papers.summary: This perspective reviews the development of right-handed D-sulfonyl-γ-AApeptides, a class of synthetic peptidomimetics designed to mimic α-helical protein structures. The authors summarize their laboratory's work using these scaffolds to target protein-protein interactions, highlighting their potential as tools for chemical biology and therapeutic applications.

papers.title: Standardizing pre-existing anti-PEG antibody detection: A key to clarifying their binding features and clinical relevance.
papers.abstract: Polyethylene glycol (PEG) is a widely used pharmaceutical excipient to improve drug solubility and prolong in vivo circulation duration. Although it was initially considered non-immunogenic, recent studies have confirmed the ubiquitous presence of anti-PEG antibodies pre-existing in human, influencing the efficacy and safety of multiple PEGylated medicines. Due to the contradictions of current anti-PEG antibody detection methods and unclear induction mechanism of human pre-existing anti-PEG antibodies, the actual prevalence, binding features, and biological effects of pre-existing anti-PEG ant
papers.summary: This paper argues that inconsistent methods for detecting pre-existing anti-PEG antibodies are a major obstacle to understanding their true prevalence and clinical impact on PEGylated drugs. It calls for standardized detection approaches to clarify how these antibodies bind and whether they meaningfully affect drug efficacy and safety.

papers.title: Subunit-dependent interfacial assembly of wheat gliadin subunits by Lycium barbarum polysaccharide underlies foam stabilization.
papers.abstract: Protein foams are governed by interfacial adsorption kinetics and film stability, yet the subunit-specific regulation of wheat gliadins by polysaccharides remains unclear. Here, the differential responses of α- and ω-gliadin to Lycium barbarum polysaccharide (LBP) were systematically elucidated by integrating interfacial tension kinetics, foaming performance, multiscale structure, and atomistic molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. Under the matched solvent conditions, α-gliadin exhibited higher foaming capacity and stability than ω-gliadin. LBP significantly enhanced the foam stability of both
papers.summary: This study shows that Lycium barbarum polysaccharide (LBP) improves the foam stability of wheat gliadin proteins, but the effect depends on the protein subunit type. By combining interfacial measurements, structural analysis, and molecular dynamics simulations, the authors found that α-gliadin forms more stable foams than ω-gliadin and that LBP interacts differently with each subunit to stabilize the interfacial film.

papers.title: Heat-time-controlled chickpea protein aggregates: structure-function-digestibility interplay and Pickering emulsion performance.
papers.abstract: This study systematically investigated the modulation effects of heating duration (0-60 min) on the structure, functional properties, and Pickering emulsion performance of chickpea protein aggregates (CPAs). CPAs heated for 30 min (CPAs-30) exhibited favorable properties: the smallest particle size (534.67 nm) and zeta potential (-26.6 mV), and enhanced colloidal stability compared to other heating durations. Further mechanistic analysis revealed that a synergistic stabilization mechanism involving enhanced hydrophobic interactions (contact angle increased from 71.75° to 77.8°, surface hydroph
papers.summary: This study examined how heating duration (0-60 min) affects the structure, function, and digestibility of chickpea protein aggregates, finding that 30 minutes of heating produced the optimal aggregates with the smallest particle size and best colloidal stability. These optimal aggregates also performed well as Pickering emulsion stabilizers, with the stabilization mechanism involving enhanced hydrophobic interactions.

papers.title: HDX-MS-Guided computational modeling for rapid and accurate antibody-antigen interface mapping.
papers.abstract: Accurate mapping of paratopes and epitopes at antibody-antigen (Ab-Ag) interfaces is essential for the rational design of therapeutic antibodies in early drug development. Traditional methods for determining high-resolution Ab-Ag complex structures, such as X-ray crystallography and cryo-electron microscopy, are labor-intensive and require substantial time and resources. Although recent computational approaches have increased throughput, prediction accuracy and reliability remain limited, particularly without experimental structural constraints. Here, we present a hydrogen-deuterium exchange m
papers.summary: This paper presents a computational modeling approach that uses hydrogen-deuterium exchange mass spectrometry (HDX-MS) data as experimental constraints to rapidly and accurately map antibody-antigen interfaces. By integrating HDX-MS measurements with computational prediction, the method improves the accuracy of paratope and epitope identification compared to purely computational approaches. This could accelerate the rational design of therapeutic antibodies by reducing reliance on labor-intensive structural methods like X-ray crystallography and cryo-EM.

papers.title: Cryo-EM structure-based discovery of etravirine as a specific inhibitor of PRMT5/pICln protein-protein interaction for prostate cancer treatment.
papers.abstract: Protein arginine methyltransferase 5 (PRMT5) is overexpressed in many cancers and correlates with poor patient survival. In prostate cancer, PRMT5 cooperates with its cofactor pICln to promote tumour growth by epigenetically activating androgen receptor (AR) expression. Using a near-atomic cryo-EM structure of PRMT5/MEP50/pICln complex, we identified a previously undefined, pICln-specific protein-protein interaction (PPI) interface on PRMT5, termed P4I. Structure-based virtual screening identified the FDA-approved compound etravirine as a binder to this site. BiFC, Co-IP, and PLA assays confir
papers.journal: Journal of enzyme inhibition and medicinal chemistry
papers.summary: Using a near-atomic cryo-EM structure of the PRMT5/MEP50/pICln complex, the authors identified a previously undefined pICln-specific protein-protein interaction interface on PRMT5 (termed P4I). Structure-based virtual screening of this site identified the FDA-approved drug etravirine as a specific inhibitor of the PRMT5/pICln interaction, with potential for treating prostate cancer by disrupting epigenetic activation of androgen receptor expression.

papers.title: Carboxylate-Ligand-Based Coordination Polymers and Metal Complexes: From Structural Diversity and Supramolecular Descriptors to Function-Oriented Design.
papers.abstract: Carboxylate-ligand-based coordination polymers and metal complexes form structurally adaptable crystalline systems, spanning discrete complexes, one-dimensional chains, two-dimensional layers, three-dimensional frameworks, and MOF-like architectures. This adaptability arises from diverse carboxylate binding modes and metal coordination preferences; auxiliary N/O donors are included only when carboxylate coordination remains central. However, the increasing availability of structural and electronic descriptors has not always been matched by equally rigorous validation of structure-function rela
papers.summary: This review surveys carboxylate-ligand-based coordination polymers and metal complexes, covering their structural diversity from discrete complexes to 3D frameworks and MOF-like architectures. It emphasizes how carboxylate binding modes and metal coordination preferences drive structural adaptability, and discusses supramolecular descriptors for function-oriented design. The authors note that the growing availability of structural and electronic descriptors has outpaced rigorous validation of structure-function relationships.

papers.title: Phospholipid-Prednisolone Conjugates for Targeted IBD Therapy: Structural Design, Synthetic Approaches, Optimization, and Computational Evaluation.
papers.abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), including Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis, is a chronic disorder characterized by persistent intestinal inflammation. Although corticosteroids such as prednisolone effectively control disease symptoms, prolonged treatment is associated with severe side effects, including immune suppression and metabolic disturbances. To enable site-specific drug delivery, four phospholipid-linker-prednisolone conjugates were designed and synthesized as prodrugs targeting the overexpression of phospholipase A2 (PLA2) in inflamed intestinal tissues. The conjugates were pr
papers.summary: This paper describes the design and synthesis of four phospholipid-linker-prednisolone prodrug conjugates intended to release the corticosteroid specifically in inflamed intestinal tissue via phospholipase A2 (PLA2) cleavage. The authors also performed computational evaluation to optimize the linker and conjugate structures for targeted IBD therapy, aiming to reduce systemic side effects of prednisolone.

papers.title: Atomic-Scale Mechanism of Titanium-Induced Frictional Removal of Silicon Carbide: A Molecular Dynamics Study.
papers.abstract: The atomic-scale mechanism of the titanium-induced frictional removal of 3C-SiC remains insufficiently understood, particularly regarding the role of interfacial chemical interactions in material removal. In this study, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations were performed to systematically investigate the interfacial reactions, atomic migration, and structural evolution during titanium friction on SiC surfaces. The results demonstrate that Ti atoms diffuse into the SiC lattice, while Si and C atoms migrate toward the Ti layer, leading to the formation and evolution of Ti-Si and Ti-C bonds at the
papers.summary: This study uses molecular dynamics simulations to reveal how titanium induces frictional removal of silicon carbide at the atomic scale. The simulations show that titanium atoms diffuse into the SiC lattice while silicon and carbon atoms migrate toward the titanium layer, forming Ti-Si and Ti-C bonds that drive material removal. The work clarifies the interfacial chemical interactions underlying this tribochemical process.

papers.title: Molecular Insights into Dynamic Relaxation in Vitrimers: Transesterification-Driven Self-Healing at the Atomistic Level.
papers.abstract: Vitrimers are covalent adaptable networks that combine the structural stability of thermosets with self-healing enabled by dynamic covalent bonds. However, the molecular-level interplay among polymerization, prescribed bond-exchange reactions (BERs), finite-time mechanical relaxation, and nanoscale interfacial recovery remains incompletely understood. Here, we employ all-atom molecular dynamics simulations with the REACTER template-based reaction algorithm to construct a Bis-GMA/2-HEMA methacrylate polymer assembly and to model temperature-dependent transesterification. The resulting structure
papers.summary: This study uses all-atom molecular dynamics simulations with a template-based reaction algorithm to model how transesterification bond-exchange reactions drive self-healing in methacrylate-based vitrimers. It reveals atomistic details of the coupling between polymerization, dynamic covalent bond exchange, and mechanical relaxation that enable nanoscale interfacial recovery.

papers.title: Dynamic Protein Structure Paradox: An Integrative Framework for Endpoint-Conditioned Evidentiary Sufficiency in Structure-to-Function Claims.
papers.abstract: Accurate coordinates for a represented protein state do not, by themselves, establish activity or any other condition-specific function. This article defines the Dynamic Protein Structure Paradox (DPSP) as the apparent conflict between structural accuracy and functional underdetermination and develops it as an integrative evidentiary assessment framework rather than a new theory or paradigm. The underlying problem has been longstanding, since structural genomics, function annotation, allostery, and disorder research each established that fold does not determine function and that function does
papers.summary: This article introduces the Dynamic Protein Structure Paradox (DPSP), the observation that accurate protein structure coordinates alone cannot establish a protein's function or activity. It proposes an integrative evidentiary framework for assessing when structure-to-function claims are sufficiently supported, rather than presenting a new theory or experimental method.

papers.title: Expired Ibrutinib as a Sustainable Corrosion Inhibitor for P110 Carbon Steel in Hydrochloric Acid: Integrated Experimental, Electrochemical, and Multiscale Computational Insights.
papers.abstract: The reuse of expired pharmaceuticals as corrosion inhibitors offers a sustainable strategy for reducing pharmaceutical waste while providing environmentally friendly alternatives to conventional inhibitors. In this work, the corrosion inhibition performance of expired ibrutinib (EIB) for P110 carbon steel in 1.0 M HCl was investigated using electrochemical techniques, mass loss measurements, surface characterization, and computational approaches. Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) revealed a progressive increase in charge-transfer resistance with increasing inhibitor concentration, w
papers.summary: This study repurposes expired ibrutinib, a pharmaceutical drug, as a corrosion inhibitor for P110 carbon steel in hydrochloric acid. Using electrochemical measurements, mass loss tests, surface characterization, and multiscale computational modeling, the authors show that increasing inhibitor concentration improves corrosion protection. The work highlights a sustainable route to reduce pharmaceutical waste while providing an eco-friendly alternative to conventional corrosion inhibitors.

papers.title: Cytotoxic Triterpenes from Argan Pulp (Argania spinosa): Isolation, In Vitro Evaluation on Cancer Cell Lines, and In Silico Studies.
papers.abstract: This study focuses on the isolation, characterization, and evaluation of cytotoxicity of triterpenes extracted from argan pulp. The unsaponifiable lipids extracted from argan pulp are separated into five fractions, two of which are triterpene fractions F2 (composed of α-amyrin, β-amyrin, lupeol, ψ-taraxasterol, taraxasterol) and F4 (erythrodiol). The extraction process utilized solvent-based methods followed by purification through column chromatography. Structural elucidation was carried out using GC-MS and NMR techniques. The cytotoxic activity of the fractions was evaluated against HepG2, M
papers.summary: This study isolated and characterized triterpenes from argan pulp, identifying fractions rich in compounds such as α-amyrin, β-amyrin, lupeol, and erythrodiol using GC-MS and NMR. The fractions showed cytotoxic activity against cancer cell lines including HepG2, with in silico studies supporting the findings. The work highlights argan pulp as a source of potential anticancer natural products.

papers.title: Fine Mapping and Candidate Gene Analysis of a Major Locus Controlling Black Seed Coat Color in Mung Bean (Vigna radiata L.).
papers.abstract: Seed coat color is an important quality trait in mung bean (Vigna radiata) and is closely associated with seed appearance, commercial value, and phytochemical composition. To investigate the genetic basis of black seed coat formation, six F2 populations were derived from reciprocal crosses between the black-seeded accession LZL115 and the green-seeded accession LZL156. Among 755 F2 plants, 559 produced black-coated seeds and 196 produced green-coated seeds, conforming to a 3:1 segregation ratio (χ2 = 0.37, p = 0.54). These results indicated that black seed coat color was dominant and consisten
papers.summary: This study mapped the genetic basis of black seed coat color in mung bean using six F2 populations from reciprocal crosses between black-seeded and green-seeded accessions. Segregation ratios indicated a single dominant locus controls the trait, and fine mapping plus candidate gene analysis narrowed the region to identify likely causal genes. The findings provide genetic markers and candidate genes useful for breeding mung bean varieties with desired seed coat colors.

papers.title: Polyphenol-Rich Opuntia ficus-indica Cladodes: An Integrated Metabolomic, In Vivo and In Silico Study Supporting Their Hypolipidemic and Hepatoprotective Effects.
papers.abstract: Background: Hyperlipidemia is a major risk factor for cardiometabolic disorders, including non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD), and is closely associated with oxidative stress. Opuntia ficus-indica (OFI) cladodes are recognized as a rich source of bioactive phytochemicals; however, the molecular mechanisms underlying their metabolic benefits remain incompletely understood. Objectives: This study aimed to comprehensively evaluate the hypolipidemic and hepatoprotective potential of a polyphenol-rich O. ficus-indica cladode extract (OCE) using an integrated approach combining in vivo evalua
papers.summary: This study combined metabolomic profiling, in vivo animal experiments, and in silico modeling to investigate how a polyphenol-rich extract from Opuntia ficus-indica cladodes reduces blood lipids and protects the liver. The extract showed hypolipidemic and hepatoprotective effects, with the integrated approach helping to clarify the molecular mechanisms behind these benefits. The findings support the potential of OFI cladodes as a natural intervention for hyperlipidemia and NAFLD.

papers.title: Asymmetric Connectivity Between Redox-Active Tyrosines and Reaction-Center Chlorophylls in Photosystem II.
papers.abstract: Photosystem II (PSII) contains several cofactors involved in light harvesting, charge separation, electron transfer, and catalysis. The initial charge separation in the reaction center of PSII creates the strongest known redox-cofactor oxidant in biology, a cationic radical distributed over a "special pair" of chlorophyll molecules (P680•+). Two redox-active tyrosines, YZ and YD, located at opposite sides of the special pair, are the principal residues that reduce this cationic radical. YZ, in turn, oxidizes the manganese cluster of the oxygen-evolving complex to drive water oxidation, whereas
papers.summary: This study examines how two redox-active tyrosine residues (YZ and YD) in Photosystem II interact with the chlorophyll special pair (P680) that drives charge separation. The authors find asymmetric connectivity between these tyrosines and the reaction-center chlorophylls, which may explain their distinct functional roles in water oxidation and electron transfer. This structural insight helps clarify the molecular basis of photosynthetic energy conversion.

papers.title: Mutation-Aware Machine Learning Framework for Predicting Binding Affinity of Nirmatrelvir Analogs Targeting Coronavirus Main Proteases.
papers.abstract: The emergence of resistance-associated mutations in coronavirus main protease (Mpro) poses a significant challenge to the development of broad-spectrum antiviral therapeutics. In this study, we improved and accelerated a mutation-aware machine learning (ML) framework to predict the binding score of Nirmatrelvir analogue ligands against wild-type and mutant MERS-CoV Mpro. A library of 15,889 Nirmatrelvir derivatives generated through systematic scaffold modification was docked against the wild-type and five variants of the Mpro, producing a total of 95,334 structural and docking score datasets
papers.summary: The authors built a mutation-aware machine learning framework to predict binding scores of 15,889 Nirmatrelvir analogs against wild-type and five mutant MERS-CoV main proteases, generating over 95,000 docking datasets. This enables rapid virtual screening of antiviral candidates that remain effective against resistance mutations.

papers.title: Pyridopyrimidines and Pyridopyrimidinones as Kinase-Targeted Anticancer Agents: Medicinal Chemistry and Mechanistic Insights.
papers.abstract: Pyridopyrimidine is an important heterocyclic scaffold widely explored in anticancer drug discovery. Its structural similarity to purine enables effective interaction with various biological targets, mainly kinases involved in cancer progression. This manuscript presents recent developments reported between 2021 and 2026, focusing on the biological evaluation, and structure-activity relationships of pyridopyrimidine derivatives. Many of these synthesized compounds act as inhibitors of key targets such as EGFR, CDK4/6, and the PI3K/mTOR pathway, which are closely associated with tumor growth, s
papers.summary: This review surveys pyridopyrimidine and pyridopyrimidinone derivatives developed between 2021 and 2026 as kinase-targeted anticancer agents. It highlights their structural resemblance to purine, their activity against targets like EGFR, CDK4/6, and PI3K/mTOR, and the structure-activity relationships guiding their optimization. The paper consolidates medicinal chemistry and mechanistic insights for this scaffold class.

papers.title: Computational prediction of a multi-epitope Human Metapneumovirus vaccine candidate through integrated reverse vaccinology and pan-genomic approaches.
papers.abstract: Human metapneumovirus (HMPV) is a primary cause of global respiratory infections yet no approved vaccine currently exists. This study computationally predicts a multi-epitope vaccine candidate using a diverse dataset of 65 HMPV sequences spanning five continents. Following the screening of lead proteins for antigenicity and virulence, fifteen highly conserved MHC-I, MHC-II and B-cell epitopes were prioritized. These were integrated with a putative L7/L12 adjuvant using optimized AAY, GPGPG, and KK linkers to design three constructs (HMPV_V1-V3). Structural validation identified HMPV-V2 as the
papers.summary: This study computationally designed multi-epitope vaccine candidates against human metapneumovirus (HMPV) by screening 65 viral sequences from five continents for conserved antigenic proteins. Fifteen conserved MHC-I, MHC-II, and B-cell epitopes were linked with an L7/L12 adjuvant to create three constructs, with structural validation identifying HMPV-V2 as the most promising candidate. The work provides a pan-genomic, reverse-vaccinology framework for HMPV vaccine development, though experimental validation remains to be done.

papers.title: Associations between serum lactate and renal dysfunction in diabetic kidney disease: An exploratory analysis integrating animal experiments, clinical cohorts, and bioinformatic approaches.
papers.abstract: Diabetic kidney disease (DKD) is a major cause of end-stage renal disease, but the metabolic changes associated with its progression are still not well understood. Lactate, traditionally regarded as a byproduct of glycolysis, has been increasingly recognized in recent studies in association with broader metabolic and regulatory processes. This study aimed to evaluate the association between serum lactate and renal dysfunction in DKD and to explore candidate molecular pathways linking lactate-associated metabolic alterations to DKD-related renal injury using animal experiments, clinical cohort
papers.summary: This study investigates whether serum lactate levels are associated with kidney dysfunction in diabetic kidney disease (DKD), combining animal experiments, clinical cohort data, and bioinformatic pathway analysis. The authors aim to identify molecular pathways linking lactate-related metabolic changes to DKD-related kidney injury. The findings suggest lactate may serve as a marker or mediator of metabolic dysregulation in DKD progression.

papers.title: Identification of differentially expressed lncRNAs and candidate ceRNA networks across Mastitis stages in Sahiwal cattle.
papers.abstract: Along with being a significant disease in dairy cattle which incurs economic loss, mastitis also affects a wide range of parameters that involve milk yield and quality. However, the role of long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) in the regulation of mastitis in distinct stages of the disease in Sahiwal cows is yet to be understood. This study characterised lncRNA expression profiles and competing endogenous RNA (ceRNA) networks across healthy, subclinical, and clinical mastitis stages using RNA-Seq data from milk somatic cells. Five biologically relevant ceRNA modules were identified: Five ceRNA modul
papers.summary: This study used RNA-Seq of milk somatic cells from Sahiwal cattle to profile long non-coding RNA expression across healthy, subclinical, and clinical mastitis stages. The authors identified five biologically relevant ceRNA (competing endogenous RNA) modules, revealing candidate lncRNA-miRNA-mRNA regulatory networks that may drive mastitis progression. These findings provide new insights into the molecular mechanisms of mastitis in an indigenous dairy breed.

papers.title: Leveraging bioinformatics approaches for drug repositioning in space radiation protection.
papers.abstract: The health effects of space radiation, primarily Galactic Cosmic Rays (GCRs), on humans remain largely unknown, with potential cardiovascular consequences posing a significant threat to astronauts on long-duration spaceflight missions. Currently, there are no established pharmacological countermeasures for GCR exposure. Drug repositioning offers a promising strategy to accelerate pharmaceutical research in space medicine. This study leverages existing bioinformatics techniques to identify and prioritize potential drug candidates associated with proteomic perturbations following simulated GCR e
papers.summary: This study applies bioinformatics approaches to identify existing drugs that could be repurposed to protect astronauts from the cardiovascular effects of galactic cosmic ray (GCR) exposure during long-duration spaceflight. By analyzing proteomic perturbations from simulated GCR exposure, the authors prioritize candidate compounds for further testing as space radiation countermeasures.

papers.title: Novel 1,4-Diazepane derivatives as amyloid-beta (Aβ) aggregation inhibitors.
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is characterized by the aggregation of amyloid-beta (Aβ) peptides, particularly Aβ42 and Aβ40, which contribute to neurotoxicity and disease progression. The development of novel small molecule inhibitors capable of preventing Aβ aggregation represents a promising therapeutic strategy. We report the design, synthesis and evaluation of a novel class of 1,4-diazepanes as anti-amyloid agents.
papers.summary: This paper reports the design, synthesis, and evaluation of a new class of 1,4-diazepane derivatives as inhibitors of amyloid-beta (Aβ) peptide aggregation, a key pathological process in Alzheimer's disease. The compounds represent a potential small-molecule therapeutic strategy aimed at preventing Aβ42 and Aβ40 aggregation and associated neurotoxicity.

papers.title: Potential hazard assessment of 6PPD-quinone in the context of ulcerative colitis: network toxicology, machine learning, transcriptomic analysis, and preliminary In vivo validation.
papers.abstract: The ubiquitous tire-derived pollutant 6PPD-quinone (6PPD-Q) poses potential systemic health risks, yet its toxicological impact on the intestinal tract, particularly in the context of ulcerative colitis (UC), remains largely unknown. This study aimed to investigate whether 6PPD-Q aggravates DSS-induced colitis and to identify candidate molecular events using integrative computational and experimental approaches.
papers.summary: This study investigates whether the tire-derived pollutant 6PPD-quinone (6PPD-Q) worsens ulcerative colitis, using network toxicology, machine learning, and transcriptomic analysis combined with preliminary in vivo validation in a DSS-induced colitis model. The authors identify candidate molecular events linking 6PPD-Q exposure to colitis aggravation, suggesting a potential environmental risk factor for intestinal inflammation.

papers.title: Integrated multi-omics analysis indicates MARCO and ZBTB20 as candidate biomarkers in rheumatoid arthritis and tuberculosis.
papers.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) patients have a clearly increased possibility to develop tuberculosis (TB). However, the common molecular background, useful diagnostic molecules, and treatment-related targets of this comorbidity are still not sufficiently explained. We attempted to search the shared genetic factors and candidate drug targets for RA and TB by an integrated multi-omics way.
papers.summary: This study integrates multiple omics datasets to identify shared molecular features between rheumatoid arthritis and tuberculosis, two conditions that frequently co-occur. The authors pinpoint MARCO and ZBTB20 as candidate biomarkers and potential drug targets linking the two diseases.

papers.title: A novel Ru(II) complex with pyrene-1-carbaldehyde hydrazone: structural, electronic, theoretical, and biological studies.
papers.abstract: A new Ru(II) half-sandwich complex, 1, containing an η6-p-cymene ligand and (E)-1-(pyren-1-ylmethylidene)hydrazine, was synthesized in good yield and characterized by FTIR, NMR, elemental analysis, and density functional theory calculations. The close agreement between experimental and theoretical FTIR, 1H NMR, and 13C NMR data confirmed the proposed structure, while geometry optimization revealed the expected pseudo-octahedral piano-stool arrangement around the Ru(II) center. QTAIM analysis indicated that the metal-ligand interactions, particularly Ru-N and Ru-arene bonds, possess partial cov
papers.summary: This paper reports the synthesis and characterization of a new ruthenium(II) half-sandwich complex bearing a pyrene-1-carbaldehyde hydrazone ligand, combining experimental techniques (FTIR, NMR, elemental analysis) with DFT calculations. The theoretical results confirm the proposed piano-stool geometry and reveal partial covalent character in the Ru-N and Ru-arene bonds. Biological studies were also performed, though the abstract does not detail their outcomes.

papers.title: Protein language model-generated enzyme sequences exhibit high stability in molecular dynamics simulations.
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have transformed protein engineering by capturing complex sequence patterns from large datasets, enabling applications such as structure prediction and functional annotation. Finenzyme applies conditional transfer learning to generate biologically plausible enzyme sequences conditioned on Enzyme Commission (EC) numbers.
papers.summary: This study evaluates enzyme sequences generated by Finenzyme, a protein language model that uses conditional transfer learning to produce sequences based on Enzyme Commission numbers. Molecular dynamics simulations show that these generated enzymes exhibit high structural stability, suggesting that language model-generated sequences can be biologically plausible and stable.

papers.title: Naringenin restores neuronal membrane electro-biophysical homeostasis: insights from EIS circuit modeling and molecular dynamics.
papers.abstract: Naringenin (NGN), a bioactive flavonoid derived from Citri Reticulatae Pericarpium, exhibits considerable neuroprotective properties. However, the precise mechanisms underlying its restoration of neuronal membranes during oxidative stress remain elusive.
papers.summary: This study investigates how naringenin, a flavonoid from citrus peel, protects neuronal membranes under oxidative stress. Using electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) circuit modeling and molecular dynamics simulations, the authors show that naringenin restores membrane electro-biophysical homeostasis, likely by stabilizing membrane structure and electrical properties. The work links a natural compound's neuroprotective effects to measurable changes in membrane biophysics.

papers.title: Molecular Dynamics Study of Supramolecular Complexes to the Carbohydrate-Cation System.
papers.abstract: It is known that calcium ions lead to aggregation of disaccharides, while magnesium ions do not. In this study, simulation results indicated that the cations primarily bind to the sulfate groups of the disaccharides.
papers.summary: This molecular dynamics study investigates how divalent cations interact with sulfated disaccharides, finding that calcium ions promote disaccharide aggregation while magnesium ions do not. The simulations show that both cations primarily bind to the sulfate groups of the disaccharides, suggesting that differences in binding geometry or hydration drive the distinct aggregation behavior.

papers.title: DBP-CanPred: a machine learning model for predicting cancer-causing mutations in DNA-binding proteins.
papers.abstract: The fundamental cellular processes, including transcriptional regulation, chromatin organization, and genome maintenance, are regulated by DNA-binding proteins (DBPs). Mutations in DBPs can alter protein-DNA interactions, leading to tumor development. However, identifying such driver mutations remains a major challenge due to limitations of experimental approaches.
papers.summary: DBP-CanPred is a machine learning model designed to predict which mutations in DNA-binding proteins are likely to drive cancer. It addresses the challenge of distinguishing cancer-causing mutations from benign ones in proteins that regulate transcription, chromatin, and genome maintenance, where experimental screening is difficult.

papers.title: Multi-state Structure Prediction of G Protein-Coupled Receptor Proteins via Prompting on AlphaFold.
papers.abstract: G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs), an essential family of transmembrane proteins, widely participate in signal transduction in organisms and have long been recognized as a major class of therapeutic targets. In structure-based drug design, high-resolution structures of GPCRs in both active and inactive states are essential for designing agonists and antagonists, respectively. However, obtaining experimental GPCR structures is costly, while homology modeling and artificial-intelligence-driven approaches including AlphaFold 2 and AlphaFold 3 often show reduced accuracy for active-state conform
papers.summary: This paper presents a method that uses prompt-based adaptation of AlphaFold to predict multiple conformational states (active and inactive) of G protein-coupled receptors, which are important drug targets. The approach addresses the limited accuracy of standard AlphaFold for active-state GPCR structures, potentially aiding structure-based design of agonists and antagonists.

papers.title: A voyage of reprogrammable metabolic bioengineering reshapes plant defense: from editing tools to synthetic systems.
papers.abstract: Metabolic bioengineering has emerged as a transformative approach for reshaping plant defense by targeting intrinsic biosynthetic pathways to enhance immunity in modern agriculture. Moving beyond proof-of-concept metabolomics to broad-spectrum programmable pathway engineering addresses gaps in plant rational design and optimizes resilience in response to diverse environmental cues. This review aims to comprehensively highlight the transition of innovative approaches to phenolics, alkaloids, flavonoids, terpenoids, and benzoxazinoids, inferring adaptive reprogramming that mediates the growth-de
papers.summary: This review surveys how metabolic bioengineering can be used to reprogram plant biosynthetic pathways—such as those producing phenolics, alkaloids, flavonoids, terpenoids, and benzoxazinoids—to strengthen plant immunity. It traces the field's shift from proof-of-concept metabolomics toward programmable, broad-spectrum pathway engineering for more resilient crops.

papers.title: PLK1/FOXM1-associated tumor-cell state and macrophage-related immune features in endometrial cancer.
papers.abstract: Polo-like kinase 1 (PLK1) and forkhead box M1 (FOXM1) have been widely studied in various cancers; however, their expression characteristics in endometrial cancer (EC) and their potential association with tumor microenvironment remodeling remain insufficiently characterized.
papers.summary: This study characterizes the expression of PLK1 and FOXM1 in endometrial cancer and links them to a specific tumor-cell state and macrophage-related immune features in the tumor microenvironment. The findings suggest that PLK1/FOXM1 activity may shape immune remodeling in endometrial cancer, potentially informing prognosis or therapeutic targeting.

papers.title: Naringenin as a dual-target modulator of RAGE-NF-κB signaling and Aβ fibrillization in Alzheimer's disease: integrated computational and experimental analyses.
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a complex neurodegenerative disorder characterized by the accumulation and aggregation of β-amyloid (Aβ) and chronic neuroinflammation mediated by the receptor for advanced glycation end products (RAGE). Current therapeutic candidates targeting RAGE signaling or Aβ aggregation continue to face challenges, including off-target toxicity, poor blood-brain barrier (BBB) penetration, and limited multi-target efficacy.
papers.summary: This study investigates naringenin, a natural flavonoid, as a potential dual-target therapeutic for Alzheimer's disease. Using integrated computational and experimental approaches, the authors show that naringenin can simultaneously modulate RAGE-NF-κB neuroinflammatory signaling and inhibit Aβ fibrillization, suggesting a multi-target mechanism that may overcome limitations of current single-target candidates.

papers.title: Nanogel-Based Precision Bone Regeneration: Rational Design, Biological Barrier Penetration, and Osteoporotic Microenvironment Remodeling.
papers.abstract: The pathogenesis of osteoporosis is primarily associated with impaired communication between osteoblasts and osteoclasts, leading to disrupted bone homeostasis. Conventional biomaterials mainly rely on macroscopic structural support and are limited in their ability to precisely regulate the complex bone microenvironment and overcome biological barriers. As representative soft matter nanoplatforms, nanogels possess unique viscoelastic mechanical properties and adaptive biointerfacial properties, offering new opportunities to overcome physical barriers within bone tissues. Moving beyond previous
papers.summary: This review discusses nanogel-based platforms for bone regeneration, focusing on their rational design, ability to penetrate biological barriers, and capacity to remodel the osteoporotic microenvironment. It argues that nanogels' viscoelastic and adaptive biointerfacial properties enable precise regulation of the complex bone microenvironment, surpassing conventional macroscopic biomaterials limited to structural support.
